samples.summary: Comment writes call NotificationService.createFromComment directly with an unvalidated, uncapped recipient list, bypassing CommentNotificationDto's ArrayMaxSize(50) and UserThrottlerGuard
samples.evidence: `ApiV1CommentsController.notify()` builds plans with `planCommentNotifications(...) as CommentNotificationDto[]` (comments.controller.ts:197-203) and hands them straight to `this.notificationService.createFromComment(actorId, plan)` (line 206). Because this is an in-process call, no `ValidationPipe` runs, so the DTO's `@ArrayMaxSize(50)` on `recipientUserIds` and `@MaxLength(2000)` on `preview` (notification.dto.ts:57-67) never apply — the `as` cast merely asserts they did. `recipientUserIds` is derived from `extractMentionedUserIds(comment.body)` (packages/sheets/src/comment/notify-plan.ts:110-113), which is unbounded, and `normalizeBody` (yorkie/comment-ops.ts:360) puts no length limit on the body. `bodyParser.json({ limit: '25mb' })` (main.ts:20,50) therefore lets a single `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/documents/:id/comments` carry ~2.5M distinct `@[a](N)` tokens. Those all reach `NotificationService.createFromComment`, which does `unique(dto.recipientUserIds)` and then `memberIdsAmong(...)` → `prisma.workspaceMember.findMany({ where: { userId: { in: <millions of ids> } } })` (notification.service.ts:123-133,432-435) BEFORE the `slice(0, MAX_RECIPIENTS)` cap at line 138. Attack: any workspace member (or any write-scoped API key, which needs no browser) posts such a comment repeatedly; the only bound is the global IP-keyed `ThrottlerGuard` at 120/min (app.module.ts:97-104), which the notification HTTP route deliberately replaced with the user-keyed `UserThrottlerGuard` for exactly this reason (user-throttler.guard.ts:8-15). Result is a Postgres/Node resource-exhaustion vector. docs/design/notifications.md explicitly acknowledges the throttler is skipped but justifies it on 'the one-comment-per-request shape', which does not bound the derived recipient fan-out.

samples.summary: No maximum length is enforced on a comment body written through the API, so an authenticated caller can permanently store 25MB per comment in the CRDT
samples.evidence: `normalizeBody` (comment-ops.ts:360-363) only checks `typeof raw === 'string'` and non-blankness; `createThread`/`reply`/`editComment` in comments.controller.ts (lines ~269, ~356, ~415) use it as their sole body validation, and `@Body() body: unknown` carries no class-validator metadata so the global `ValidationPipe` (main.ts:65-69) is a no-op for it. With `BACKEND_JSON_BODY_LIMIT` defaulting to `25mb` (main.ts:20) a write-scoped API key can push a 25MB string into `sheets[tab].comments[...]` / `root.comments[...]` on every request, and comments are never garbage-collected or size-checked anywhere. This inflates the Yorkie document (and every collaborator's snapshot download) without bound.
searchedFor: read packages/sheets/src/comment/thread.ts assertNonEmpty reference in diff

samples.summary: parseImages accepts an arbitrary `src` string with no scheme or origin validation, letting an API caller plant third-party or data: URLs into worksheet content that every viewer's browser then fetches
samples.evidence: `parseImage` validates `anchor` against `parseRef` and the numeric fields, but `src` is only `requireString(i.src, 'src')` (worksheet-images.ts:55) and is stored verbatim by `ApiV1WorksheetImagesController.setImages` (worksheet-images.controller.ts:91-110). The editor cannot produce such a value — it can only reference an uploaded workspace image — but `PUT .../tabs/:tabId/images` can. `image-object-layer.tsx:195-216` renders it into `` for every viewer, so a member (or a stolen write-scoped key) can turn a shared spreadsheet into a beacon that reports each viewer's IP/User-Agent to an attacker-controlled host, or embed an unbounded `data:` payload. `share-image-url.ts:27-42` only gates *token appending*, not the fetch itself, so no existing control stops this. The same laxity exists for slides/board element `data.src` (docs-content.controller.ts assertValidElementData does not check src), so this is consistent with prior behaviour rather than novel — hence minor.
searchedFor: grep fetch(/axios in packages/backend/src for server-side SSRF

samples.summary: Caller-supplied documentId is reflected verbatim into error messages
samples.evidence: `loadCommentableType` interpolates the raw route parameter into the 400 body: `"${documentId}" is a "${meta.type}" document.` (comments.controller.ts:133-137); `ApiV1SlidesController.assertSlidesDocument` does the same (slides.controller.ts:~69-73). The response is JSON so this is not directly XSS, but it echoes unsanitised attacker input into a message that clients commonly render, and it also confirms the persisted `type` of documents in the workspace. Low impact; noted for hardening only.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim is present as described. comments.controller.ts:197-206 casts planCommentNotifications output to CommentNotificationDto[] and calls notificationService.createFromComment in-process, so the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65-72) never runs and the DTO's @ArrayMaxSize(50)/@IsInt each/@MaxLength(2000) (notification.dto.ts:57-67) do not apply — those bind only on the HTTP route notification.controller.ts:66-70. recipientUserIds comes from extractMentionedUserIds (notify-plan.ts:109-121), which is uncapped and additionally O(n^2) via ids.includes (mentions.ts:83-91). normalizeBody (comment-ops.ts:360-363) imposes no length limit and no other cap exists in comments.controller.ts, while bodyParser.json accepts 25mb (main.ts:20,49-57). In notification.service.ts the unbounded list reaches memberIdsAmong -> prisma.workspaceMember.findMany({ where: { userId: { in: ... } } }) (lines 126-129, 432-435) BEFORE the .slice(0, MAX_RECIPIENTS=20) cap at line 138, so the cap is downstream of the expensive query. The only rate limit on this path is the IP-keyed global ThrottlerGuard 120/min (app.module.ts:97-104,129); the user-keyed UserThrottlerGuard (user-throttler.guard.ts:17-27) is not among the guards on this controller (comments.controller.ts:113). No guard elsewhere bounds body size or mention count, so I found nothing that makes this unreachable. Requires an authenticated workspace member or write-scoped API key, which limits the attacker set but does not refute the vector; unbounded attacker-controlled input into a Prisma IN list plus an O(n^2) parse is unsafe input handling / resource exhaustion within the security lane.

mergedFrom.summary: `tabId` route param is used as an unfiltered object key for both the existence check and the write, giving a prototype-pollution shape (`PUT .../tabs/__proto__/images`)

finding.summary: User-controlled `:tabId` is used directly as an object key and then written into (`ws.images = {}`), so a request with `tabId=__proto__` can reach an assignment onto `Object.prototype` if the root ever behaves like a plain object
finding.evidence: `setImages` takes `:tabId` straight from the URL (Express URL-decodes, so `%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F` → `__proto__`) and does `root.sheets?.[tabId]` in `worksheetOrThrow` (line 51-57). On a plain JS object `sheets['__proto__']` returns `Object.prototype` — truthy — so the NotFound guard passes and `doc.update` then executes `ws.images = {}` followed by `ws.images[image.id] = image` (lines 97-98), writing attacker-controlled data onto `Object.prototype`. Against a real Yorkie object proxy the outcome depends on the SDK's `get` trap (the SDK is not installed in this tree, so I could not confirm which way it falls); the controller's own spec harness uses a plain object, which is the shape where this is exploitable. Note the identical pattern already exists pre-change in `worksheet-charts.controller.ts:106-110`, so this is a new instance of an existing pattern rather than a new class. A cheap fix is to reject any `tabId` that is not present in `root.tabOrder`, or to use `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(sheets, tabId)`.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. worksheet-images.controller.ts:53-60 resolves the raw route param `tabId` via `root.sheets?.[tabId]` and gates only on truthiness (`if (!worksheet) throw NotFound`); setImages (lines 106-113) then executes `ws.images = {}` and `ws.images[image.id] = image` on whatever that lookup returned. No guard validates tabId anywhere on the path: WorkspaceScopeGuard (workspace-scope.guard.ts:32-46) checks only workspace membership, assertSheetDocument (lines 40-51) only the document type, and ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard only the key scope. The repository itself documents this exact pattern as unsafe: worksheet-structure.controller.ts:80-113 states a bare truthiness check is bypassable because the Yorkie proxy get trap returns truthy *functions* for getID/toJSON/toJS/toJSForTest/toString ("walked past a bare `if (!worksheet)`"), and that `__proto__` is truthy on a plain object; that controller therefore uses the membership test `safeWorksheetRecordKeys(sheets).includes(tabId)` (line 109), pinned by worksheet-structure.controller.spec.ts:70-81. The images controller uses neither helper (grep: safeWorksheetRecordKeys is imported only by the structure controller). I could not refute production reachability: YorkieService.withDocument (yorkie.service.ts:36-73) always builds a real yorkie.Document, but @yorkie-js/sdk is not installed in this tree (no node_modules/@yorkie-js/**), so the get trap's handling of `__proto__` is unverifiable here — and even if `__proto__` is neutralised, `tabId=toString` still passes this guard per the repo's own comment. Unvalidated attacker-controlled object key reaching a write path is in the security lane (unsafe input handling / prototype pollution), so no refutation ground applies.
